correctness.rationale: The iid delay conditional second-moment map is derived on the exact symmetric 2×2 covariance cone. Its determinant is h(2−h−ph²), and positivity ensures its spectral radius is a nonnegative eigenvalue; the local Perron derivative is −2 and continuity excludes another crossing. At the boundary an eigenvalue is one and beyond the determinant has the wrong sign for Schur stability. Rank-one deterministic initial states span covariance space, ensuring the stated all-initial-pairs quantifier. For the (p,h)=(1/4,3/2) example a weighted max norm and strong law give a negative almost-sure logarithmic growth bound, while an exact rational generating function has a unique dominant positive pole (verified characteristic polynomial) and positive coefficient, forcing exponential expected-error growth. Exact symbolic verifier and finite exhaustive small-n independent checks passed; finite checks are not used to prove continuum statements.

value.rationale: The impact of genuinely random staleness on a numerical gradient solver is a motivated optimization question. The exact sharp step ceiling decreases continuously from 2 to 1 as stale probability increases, replacing conservative upper bounds or numerical stability diagrams with a complete natural one-dimensional model. More importantly, the same explicit solver/step/delay law has exponentially decaying iterates on almost every sample path while expected quadratic loss diverges exponentially, proving a structurally significant risk-assessment distinction. This is not a named-parameter substitution or a tiny improvement and does not claim broader high-dimensional performance.
